title: Ra’az Borg
summary: Bilingual grappling website for RA’AZ BORG in Quito. I extended the existing site with athlete registration and a staff review workflow.
context: RA’AZ BORG organizes grappling events in Quito, Ecuador.

image.alt: Ra’az Borg squad image used in the combat-sports website
image.caption: Squad artwork from the original website.

problem: A distinctive sports identity needs a coherent website across fighter profiles, events, media and merchandise. The interface must preserve its visual character while remaining usable on smaller screens and across English and Spanish content.
contribution: I extended the team’s existing website with a bilingual athlete portal backed by Supabase Auth and PostgreSQL. My changes were merged into the original project repository.

approach.title: Connect the site sections
approach.body: Shared navigation connects the athlete portal with fighter profiles, events, media and the shop.

approach.title: Reuse styling and interaction logic
approach.body: A shared css/style.css file supplies responsive presentation, while js/main.js handles interface behavior. The visible code includes mobile navigation, scroll reveals, animated tickers and other page interactions.

approach.title: Support bilingual navigation
approach.body: An English/Spanish toggle uses browser storage to retain the visitor’s language selection. The interface connects content translation with the same shared navigation and presentation system.

approach.title: Support athlete registration
approach.body: Athletes can register at raazborg.com, sign in and check their application status. Authorized staff can review submissions.

outcome: Athletes can register at raazborg.com, sign in and check their application status. Authorized staff can review submissions.
learning: Work on an existing design system is easiest to assess when inherited features and new modifications are clearly separated. That provenance makes both technical review and a portfolio account more useful.
limitations: The original project supplied the visual identity and core website. My contribution builds on that foundation.

evidence.title: Original squad artwork
evidence.body: The squad image is part of the existing site’s identity. It is labeled as a source asset rather than presented as a screenshot of a newly developed interface.
